title: Introduce RAG Scenario Simulator quickstart (scratchpad + live assertions)
author: Priya Nair
description: This PR adds a compact RAG Scenario Simulator quickstart designed for engineers and technical PMs to author, iterate, and evaluate RAG scenarios locally. Motivation: many teams need a lightweight, reproducible harness that captures prompt/response pairs, step-level assertions, and telemetry probes without the overhead of full infra. The quickstart provides: 1) a Typescript 'scratchpad' runner that can replay scripted scenarios against a Redwood-hosted model or a local mock; 2) a live assertions DSL for writing deterministic checks (exact match, semantic similarity, token-budget assertions); 3) embedded telemetry probes that emit synthetic spans and metrics compatible with the Redwood Console; 4) a devcontainer and npm scripts to get started in <5 minutes. Changeset highlights: new quickstart under quickstarts/rag-sim-scratchpad/, an example scenario set (faq_search, multi_tool_booking), a small local mock server for deterministic test runs, CI workflow to lint and smoke-run scenarios, and docs/README with authoring guide and assertion examples. How to run: 1) clone repo, cd sources/github/redwood-quickstarts/quickstarts/rag-sim-scratchpad, 2) npm ci && npm run devcontainer:up (or npm start), 3) edit scenarios/*.json for custom flows, 4) npm run assert to evaluate. Checklist: - [x] quickstart code + examples - [x] devcontainer and npm tasks - [x] lightweight mock server for CI - [x] docs and examples - [x] CI smoke job verifying 2 scenarios - [x] telemetry probe emitters wired to console schema. Related: ENG-2148 tracks evaluator improvements, PM-512 product request for reproducible authoring. No breaking changes. This PR is intended to be a standalone developer example that can be cherry-picked into internal training and onboarding materials.
